| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Format | Standard (Reality Fracture, set code `fra`, plus Standard dual lands) |
| Colors | White, blue, black (Esper) |
| Archetype | Empower combo: every empower spell is a Jace token, and one Horror makes those tokens unkillable and draining |
| Size | 60 cards, 24 lands, 36 spells and creatures |
| Primary win | Attrition drain: with `Sanctum Lurker` out, each planeswalker gains "[+2]: deal 1 damage to each opponent and you gain 1 life" |

| Land as win condition | `Theorist's Sanctum`, an Island that empowers Jace 2 every turn, feeding both the drain count and the twenty-five-loyalty threshold |

Reality Fracture is Standard-legal, but every card in the set still carries no `arena_id` in the card data. The import list at the end becomes playable on Arena once the set is enabled there.

# Overview

Empower is Reality Fracture's loyalty mechanic. "Empower Jace N" puts N loyalty counters on a Jace you control, and if you do not control one it first creates a blue Jace planeswalker token with "[−1]: Surveil 1" and "[−3]: Draw a card". Every empower card is therefore both a loyalty pump and a planeswalker, and planeswalkers are what this list counts.

`Sanctum Lurker` is the hinge. The 3/2 for `{2}{B}` empowers 1 on entry, keeps your planeswalkers out of the graveyard when they hit 0 loyalty, and grants them "[+2]: This planeswalker deals 1 damage to each opponent and you gain 1 life." A Jace token can be spent all the way down and stay on the battlefield, and every planeswalker becomes a repeatable one-point drain.

The Ways are the payload. `Way of the Mentor` empowers 5 and turns every point of life gain into a loyalty counter on each planeswalker, which loops with the drain. `Way of the Cryomancer` empowers 5 and gives your planeswalkers "[−3]: the next instant or sorcery you cast this turn is copied". `Way of the Healer` empowers 5 and gives them "[−2]: create a 2/2 Cadet, surveil 1". Because loyalty never actually runs out here, the deck plays like an annuity: pay counters in, collect damage and cards every turn, and the principal comes back.

# Approach

## Game plan in three phases

1. **Turns 1-2, set the table.** `Liliana the Faultless` gains a life every time another creature or planeswalker enters, a trigger that pays off through `Way of the Mentor`. Sequence lands so the Annex cycle arrives untapped: `Fatehold Annex`, `Theorix Annex` and `Meticulous Commons` need a planeswalker, `Deserted Beach` and `Shipwreck Marsh` need two other lands.
2. **Turns 3-5, deploy the engine.** `Sanctum Lurker` first if the board allows; it converts every later empower into a permanent. Then a Way — `Way of the Mentor` by default, because five loyalty on a fresh token is already a four-turn clock. `Mindseeker Oculus` and `Protege's Awakening` are the burst empowers (4 and 6 counters), `Fatehold Charm` is the cheap one that also draws.
3. **Turns 5-7, collect.** With the Lurker plus two or three planeswalkers, every turn is 2-4 damage and 2-4 life for free, and each life gain adds a loyalty counter to every planeswalker. At twenty-five loyalty among Jaces, `Jace, Reality Sculptor` exiles the opponents' libraries down to one card each.

## Curve and mana

One card costs one mana, ten cost two, fourteen cost three, nine cost four and two cost five. The deck wants three lands and a three-drop, so the curve is deliberately flat: `Sanctum Lurker`, the Ways and `Your Fate Ends Here` all sit at three, which is where the deck's first real turn happens.

Twenty-four lands support a deck whose top of curve is two five-drops, `Jace, Reality Sculptor`, plus the four-mana Ways. Sources: twenty blue, twelve white, eight black. Black is the thinnest colour and only pays for `Sanctum Lurker` and `Way of the Necromancer`, so a hand with one `Shipwreck Marsh` or `Meticulous Commons` is enough; do not keep a hand that needs double blue and black together before turn four.

# Gameplay strategy

## Early game

Open on `Liliana the Faultless` or a tapland-free two-land start with `Fatehold Charm` up. The ideal first four turns are land, Liliana, `Sanctum Lurker`, then `Way of the Mentor` with two mana left for `Countersculpt`. Do not trade the Lurker for a random 2/2: without it, planeswalkers die at 0 loyalty and the whole engine becomes fair. Against aggro, `Fatehold Charm` mode three (+1/+2 to the team) is a real combat trick, and `Way of the Healer` Cadets are perfect blockers that also feed `Way of the Necromancer`.

## Mid game and the combo turn

The engine turn looks like this: Lurker in play, two or three planeswalkers, and a Way. Activate each planeswalker's "+2" drain ability — that is one damage per opponent and one life per activation, and each life gain triggers `Way of the Mentor`, which adds a loyalty counter to every planeswalker you control. The counters you just spent come back as growth on the others.

The burst turn uses `Way of the Cryomancer`. Because the Lurker keeps a 0-loyalty planeswalker alive, a Jace token at 3 or more loyalty can pay "[−3]: copy your next instant or sorcery" and drop to 0 without dying. Activate the copy ability on two or three planeswalkers, then cast `Protege's Awakening`: each copy empowers 6 and draws a card, which routinely means twenty-plus loyalty across the board in one turn. Loyalty abilities are sorcery-speed and once per turn per permanent, and each copy goes on the stack above the spell it copies, so countering the original does not stop the copies.

## Win condition 2 — the mill finish

`Jace, Reality Sculptor` enters at 5 loyalty. Its +1 empowers X where X is the number of Islands you control (four `Island` plus two `Theorist's Sanctum` make that 2-6 depending on board). At twenty-five or more loyalty among Jaces you control, its 0 ability exiles all but the bottom card of each opponent's library: they draw one card, then lose on their next draw step.

Twenty-five is not a high bar here. Two Ways and a `Protege's Awakening` put 16 loyalty on the board by themselves, and Jace's own +1 adds 2 or more each turn after that. If the drain is already winning, use the mill against lifegain or a stalled board.

## Mulligan guide

Keep two or three lands with `Sanctum Lurker`, or any hand with a Way plus three lands. Keep `Liliana the Faultless` plus two lands when the rest of the hand has a three-drop. Ship one-land hands, all-tapland draws, and hands with no white source — `Way of the Mentor` and `Way of the Healer` are the best cards in the deck and both need white.

## Key interactions and edge cases

- `Sanctum Lurker` stops the state-based action that would put a 0-loyalty planeswalker into the graveyard. It does not let you activate a minus ability you cannot pay for: a Jace token at 2 loyalty cannot use its [−3], it has to be grown first.
- The Jace tokens empower creates are not legendary, so several coexist. `The Theorist` and `Jace, Reality Sculptor` are legendary — playing a second copy of either kills the first, so hold the spare.
- The "+2" drain applies to every planeswalker, including the two real Jaces and `Ajani Resolute`, so the drain count equals your planeswalker count.
- `Ajani Resolute`'s 0 ability gains 1 life and grows Ajani through its own trigger, which also fires `Way of the Mentor`; with the Lurker it can sit at 0 loyalty indefinitely.
- `Countersculpt` needs a Jace on the battlefield or a Jace card in hand for the behold cost, otherwise it costs `{2}{U}{U}` instead of `{U}{U}`.
- `Theorist's Sanctum` enters tapped unless you behold a Jace, and `Your Fate Ends Here` cannot kill a permanent with mana value 2 or less — `Fatehold Charm` mode two bounces those.
- `Plan for All Outcomes` triggers on your first noncreature spell each turn only, so cast a Way or a Charm before a creature.
- Do not attack with the Lurker into open mana if it is your only copy: without it planeswalkers die at 0 loyalty and the engine becomes fair.

## Matchups

| Opponent | Plan |
|---|---|
| Aggro | Trade early with `Your Fate Ends Here`, block with Cadets, then stabilise: once the Lurker and one Way are down you gain more life per turn than they can deal |
| Control | Do not overextend into a sweeper. Hold the second `Jace, Reality Sculptor` and deploy it the turn you can activate the 0 ability; `Countersculpt` protects the burst turn |
| Midrange | Out-grind them: the drain is uncounterable once the Lurker is in play, and every removal spell they spend on a token is a card the engine replaces |
| Lifegain | Race with the mill finish; twenty-five loyalty arrives faster than their life total matters |
